title: Why Sunday
hookLine: most Christians gather on Sunday, the day of the resurrection; Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday
carry: the first day, a new start

lines: THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.
cards: A town called Troas, on the coast of what's now Turkey. Evening, the first day of the week, and a group of Christians is crammed into an upstairs room lit with oil lamps.
The book of Acts says: "And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them." And Paul keeps going. Until midnight.
A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, gets sleepier and sleepier, and falls from the third story to the ground. Paul runs down, wraps his arms around him, and says, he's alive.

Then everyone goes back upstairs, eats, and keeps talking until dawn. A scare with a happy ending, and it quietly shows something: Christians were already gathering on the first day of the week. Today's word is its name.

teach.h: THE TOMB, ON THE FIRST DAY.
teach.b: The Lord's Day. Why the first day? Because all four Gospels say the tomb was found empty on it.
John begins: "The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre." Sunday morning. So early Christians gave that day a new name.
In Revelation, John says, "I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day."
In Greek, kyriake, the Lord's. The name stuck. In modern Greek, Sunday is still Kyriaki; in Spanish it's domingo, in Italian domenica, both from the Latin for the Lord's.
In Russian, the word for Sunday simply means resurrection. Some early Christian writers called Sunday the eighth day.

teach.h: THE EIGHTH DAY, A NEW CREATION.
teach.b: The week of creation ends on the seventh; the resurrection starts a new creation, a new first day. So for them, Sunday isn't the sabbath moved over by one. It's a new start.
Later, the emperor Constantine made Sunday a legal day of rest in the Roman Empire. Not all Christians keep Sunday.
Seventh-day Adventists and Seventh Day Baptists worship on Saturday, because the commandment names the seventh day, and they keep it as written.
For Catholics and Orthodox Christians, Sunday worship is expected of the faithful; Protestant churches gather on it too. The day differs. The idea underneath is shared: one day, set apart.

how: Christians gather for worship on Sunday, the day of the resurrection, and some keep it as a day of rest; Seventh-day Adventists and Seventh Day Baptists worship and rest on Saturday, the seventh day.

games.q: you're in Troas. Paul has preached until midnight. a young man named Eutychus is sitting in the window, getting very sleepy. what happens?
o: he slips out quietly and goes home.
he falls asleep and falls three floors.
he stands up and preaches next.
games.why: he falls, Paul runs down and embraces him, and says he's alive. then they eat and talk until dawn.

practice: Look ahead at the coming week for one hour you could set apart, Sunday morning, Saturday afternoon, a weekday evening, and picture filling it with something that restores you, not chores or errands: worship, a walk, a long meal, a nap, time with someone you love.
If you pray, offer that hour to God ahead of time; if you don't, simply promise it to yourself.
